e29 - Security Vulnerability Fixes (2026-06 audit)
API-key path: in ResolveAPIKey flow set the resolved key's org_id into the same JWT-claims/context channel so programmatic access is equally scoped.

In main.go add a small bridge middleware orgBridge(next) that reads auth.OrgIDFromContext and, when present, wraps ctx with api.WithOrgID; apply it to protectedAPI only (/api/collections/, /api/sql). Reason for depth: the bridge is the one allowed seam between two packages' private context keys.

Add helpers signState(state, secret) and verifyState(value, secret) using hmac/SHA256 over the random state, encoding as "state.hex(mac)". Reason for depth: HMAC binds the cookie to the server secret so it can't be forged; two tiny funcs, no new type.
Fail closed: in auth.Middleware, if claims.OrgID == 0 return 403 {\"error\":\"no organization\"} (after email-verify check). Existing tokens without org are forced to re-auth.
Regression: valid non-admin token to GET /api/auth/users returns 403 and no user list; admin token still returns the list.
Integration: callback with valid code but no/wrong state cookie returns 400 and sets NO token cookie (use existing googleVerifier stub pattern).
In handleUsers (~523): read role via UserRoleFromContext; if != admin return 403 {\"error\":\"forbidden\"} before querying. When org isolation is live, scope the SELECT to the caller's org.

Scope results to the caller's org: reject queries whose target tables carry an org_id column unless an org filter is enforced; simplest concrete form — wrap the user query as SELECT * FROM (<q>) WHERE org_id = ? when the result set exposes org_id, else allow only sqlite_master/PRAGMA introspection.
Table-driven isolation test in api: seed records for org A and org B; assert a ctx with org A's id cannot list/get/update/delete org B's record (list excludes them, get/update/delete return 403/404).
Defense-in-depth in handleSQL (~455): if role from context != admin, return 403 before parsing the query. (api reads role via the bridge-injected value or an exported accessor; do NOT trust client.)
In auth.Middleware (~290) add ctx = WithValue(ctx, ctxOrgID, claims.OrgID), and export auth.OrgIDFromContext(ctx)(int64,bool). Add ctxOrgID contextKey.

Expose api role access: read role via a shared context. Add auth.RequireAdmin(next) middleware that 403s when UserRoleFromContext != admin; apply it to the /api/sql route in main.go. Reason for depth: reusable admin gate, mirrors existing handleUserByID role check.

Add OrgID int64 to the JWT claims struct; set it in createJWT signature and all call sites (login, register-then-login, google callback, refresh). Update verifyJWT to read it. Reason for depth: claims are the existing identity channel — no new lookup path.

In handleGoogleOAuth (~599): after generateID(), set cookie oauth_state = signState(state, a.secret) with HttpOnly, Path=/, SameSite=Lax, Secure=(r.TLS!=nil), MaxAge=600; keep sending the raw state in the Google URL.
On the success path, clear the oauth_state cookie (MaxAge=-1) right before setting the token cookie.

In handleGoogleCallback (~616): read query state and the oauth_state cookie; if cookie missing OR verifyState fails OR decoded state != query state, return 400 {\"error\":\"invalid state\"} BEFORE calling verifier.Verify.
e53 - Deploy — Process Supervisor (Runner/Instance seam)
resumeCandidates builds Specs from running rows and calls Supervisor.Run; host guaranteed registered on resume
Supervisor.supervise: Spawn → register host → Wait → backoff → re-Spawn, driven by FakeRunner + FakeClock
nextBackoff(attempt) = jitter(min(cap, base*factor^attempt)); base 1s, factor 2, cap 60s; full jitter
Explicit Stop(grace) is distinguished from a crash — Supervisor does not respawn after an intentional stop
Existing safety-net tests unaffected — runner.go adds interface types only, no Deploy struct modifications
triggerDeploy builds a Spec and calls Supervisor.Run for both static and process apps
Crash-loop trip: status→failed, UnregisterDeploymentHost(host), emit deploy.crash_looped with remediation hint
isCrashLooping(history, now) — N=5 restarts within window T=60s → true; named constants exposed as flags (no magic numbers)

components/deploy/supervisor_fakes_test.go (package deploy) — FakeInstance(waitErr error, stopCh); FakeRunner(queue []*FakeInstance) Spawn pops next; FakeClock(Sleeps []time.Duration); TestFakeRunnerSpawnsScriptedInstances drives [crash,crash,ok] sequence

e28 - Delete Deployment

Add DELETE handler in handleDeployByID: look up deployment by id (404 if missing); if status is pending or building return 409 (build in progress — caller should redeploy instead of delete); if running, kill process via d.processes map (SIGTERM) or deregister the static host from DeploymentHostRegistry; delete build directory from d.buildsDir/<id>/; evict in-memory deploy logs via d.deleteDeployLogs(id); execute DELETE FROM deployments WHERE id = ?; return 204 No Content. Guard: if the deployment is the only running deploy for its repo_id, still allow deletion (the site will show "no deployment" rather than silently break).

Add a Delete column to the deployments table in SiteDetailPage.tsx. Each row gets a small "Delete" Button (variant="ghost", size="sm") that is disabled (and shows a tooltip "Build in progress") when d.status is pending or building. On click, show an inline confirmation row or window.confirm dialog asking "Delete deployment from [date]? This cannot be undone." On confirm, call DELETE /api/deployments/{d.id}, then reload the deployments list. Show a brief error message if the request fails.
